details:
Q1: What signal should prove that an `[E2E ...]` issue really is a release-gate fixture before alerts are silenced? In every option, if the signal is missing or can't be read, alerts stay on.
Choices:
A) The title prefix plus the issue author's `author_association` is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, read from the issue payload the step already fetched. No extra API call and no change to the release gate. This matches the trusted-association pattern used elsewhere, and it still works in consumer test repos whose token account may differ. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The title prefix plus the issue author is exactly the account behind `GH_PAT`, found with one `GET /user` call. This is the strictest option. But a consumer test repo whose fixture-creating token is a different account would then send alerts on every release run.
C) The title prefix plus an `e2e-smoke-test` label that `test-and-mark-stable.yml` adds when it creates each fixture issue. This needs changes to the gate's three issue-creation sites, and anyone with triage permission could also apply the label.
Q2: Which title-based alert-silencing sites are in scope?
Choices:
A) Only the cited line, `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:129`.
B) The cited line plus the same check in `clarify.yml:510`, both using the same provenance check. Only the alert silencing changes; the low-reasoning smoke tuning stays based on the title. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Everything in B, plus the `implement.yml:142/1672` alert silencing, plus the tracking-parent check at `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:150`. That check reads `Tracking issue: #N` from an issue body the author controls, then matches `^[Orchestrator] E2E ` against the referenced issue's title.
